thread:
anika: Heads-up: APAC GPU pools are noisy after we enabled mixed MIG+timeslice on raptor-apac-frac.
jorge: Saw that. What's the symptom? pods Pending or node failures?
anika: Pods Pending with Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu then nodes created and fail with ENI quota errors. CNI logs show "AttachNetworkInterface: EnilimitExceeded" on new instances.
mei: Do we have the exact nodepool name? I want to check CA events and instance type.
anika: raptor-apac-frac, instances are c7g-like-48 (hypothetical) we picked for cost+vCPU. ENI per-instance is low for that family in APAC.
ops-bot: quota-monitor: APAC ENI usage now 46/50 in apac-south-1. Sending alert to @cloud-ops.
jorge: That explains it. Fractional MIG and time-slicing increased pod density -> more pod IPs per node -> ENI exhausted.
mei: Also saw the CNI hitting cloud API rate limits, lots of 429s in a short window. When CA brings many nodes up they try to create pod sandboxes en masse.
ryan: CA behavior? Is it repeatedly scaling up because pods remain Pending?
anika: CA logs show scale-up, nodes join but CNI fails so nodes marked NotReady then CA scales down quickly. We get churn and double billing.
mei: Short-term: mark the pool unschedulable. Taint or cordon new nodes and pause rollout of fractional profile.
jorge: I'd add lowering kubelet max pods to reduce ENI consumption per node temporarily (if instance supports more IPs via secondary ENIs we can enable later).
cloud-ops: we can request an ENI quota bump but that takes days. Quick fix: switch nodepool to larger instance family with higher ENI count, or reduce pods-per-node by using fewer MIG slices.
anika: Done: applied taint node.kubernetes.io/fractional-unsafe=true:NoSchedule on raptor-apac-frac and set autoscaler max=2 until we stabilize.
ryan: Also change CA expander to "least-waste" for GPU pools? right now it's picking wide instance types that worsen ENI spread.
mei: Good call. Also we should increase cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-delay-after-add to avoid tearing down nodes that are still recovering from CNI errors.
jorge: For rollout policy: flag feature as gated by per-AZ ENI headroom check. If ENI headroom < X, don't enable high-density pools.
anika: Logged ticket INFRA-2201 with logs + commands to revert MIG profile. Included runbook steps: 1) taint pool 2) set autoscaler max 2 3) move deployments to raptor-apac-dedicated 4) request quota bump.
ops-bot: action-log: INFRA-2201 created and linked. Notifying @oncall.
cloud-ops: We'll open quota request and evaluate reserved instances in apac-south-1 to reduce spot churn.
ryan: Long term we should:  - prefer instance families with higher ENI per vCPU  - add an admission webhook to block fractional GPU pods unless nodepool label exists  - update CNI to backoff on cloud API 429s and batch ENI attachments
mei: Also consider IPAM change: move some workloads to hostNetwork=true where appropriate (intra-node services) and enable secondary IPs per pod feature where supported.
anika: If you see "failed to create pod sandbox: attach ENI failed" message, taint that pool immediately and follow runbook.
jorge: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and include a matrix of MIG-slice -> expected pods-per-node -> ENI need per instance type.
cloud-ops: acknowledging, taking ENI bump request and will advise on instance family recommendations.
ryan: thanks. After quota is resolved let's re-run a small canary with 5 pods and monitor CNI attach rates.
mei: +1, and add circuit-breaker on rollout to stop if >20% Pending for 5m.
anika: Thanks team. Rolling back the fractional rollout in prod now.
